clue.text: Soldier carrying a blue blouse

indicators.note: carrying means the soldier holds the other pieces inside him

parts.note: GI is the usual crossword soldier, an American private
blue jokes are ribald, coarse or smutty

explanation.surface: A soldier is wearing a blue shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' tempts you towards the Italian general himself, which is apt since the blouse is named after his red shirts; 'carrying' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A garibaldi is a loose high-necked woman's shirt modelled on the red shirts of Garibaldi's followers.

clue.text: Crew board — using this?

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers
a plank is a board of wood

explanation.surface: Passengers and crew climb aboard by some means.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, a crew boards a ship using this.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangplank is the movable walkway by which people get on and off a vessel.

clue.text: Much of New Zealand city employed in production of helicopter part

indicators.note: much of means most of the city's name is kept and the end dropped

parts.note: Rotorua is a city on New Zealand's North Island

explanation.surface: A New Zealand city takes part in making helicopters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much of' drops UA from ROTORUA; 'employed in production of' is a long link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating set of blades that lifts a helicopter.

clue.text: Make a determined effort to fasten the top

definitions.meaning: to set to work vigorously, to knuckle down
to do up the buckle at the top, closing it

explanation.definitionFit: Knuckle down and get going; and to strap something shut.

clue.text: Beetle badly astray, traversing one lane

indicators.note: astray means the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
a lane is a road, abbreviated RD

explanation.surface: A beetle goes badly off course while crossing a single lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' is fodder, not the anagram signal; 'astray' shuffles BADLY with I and RD.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybird is a small red spotted beetle.

clue.text: Fungus is esoteric stuff when it comes up

parts.note: an in-joke is esoteric, shared by insiders

indicators.note: comes up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to stuff is to pack

explanation.surface: A fungus is obscure material when it sprouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it comes up' reverses PACK to KCAP below IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ink cap is a mushroom whose gills dissolve into black liquid.

clue.text: Herb the poet put in the pot

definitions.text: Herb the poet put in the pot

parts.words: Herb the poet put in the pot
parts.note: a literary allusion: Keats wrote of Isabella, who hid her murdered lover's head in a pot and grew this herb over it

explanation.walkthrough: The poem is Keats's 'Isabella, or the Pot of Basil'; the herb is both what grows in the pot and what the poet put there in his title.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's poem title names this sweet herb as the plant growing in Isabella's pot.

clue.text: Get lost and ask somebody …

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
one means a person, someone

explanation.surface: Telling someone to go away while asking someone else a question, carried on in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the surface on into 7 down; the wordplay ends here.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old command to leave, like 'clear off'.

clue.text: … a question, in petition to a sect that's fastidious

indicators.note: in means the question letter goes inside the petition word

parts.note: to sue is to petition, as in suing for peace
Q is the abbreviation for question
the Amish are a religious sect in America

explanation.surface: A fussy person poses a question in a plea to a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 6 down's surface; 'in' is the container signal, and 'that's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeamish means easily offended or overscrupulous, fussy about details.

clue.text: Church supporting G.P.

annotationWithheld.why: Church supporting G.P. (5) for LEECH: CH supports LEE, which can only come from 'G.' (General Lee) while 'G.P.' is also the definition, so one word does two jobs

clue.text: A plain cake is seen

definitions.meaning: a cake left plain has no icing, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NOT ICED and it describes a plain cake; read whole it means seen, with 'is' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Observed or spotted; and a cake with no topping is one lacking icing.

clue.text: Thin coat — in the past, you said, deer went around without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the turned deer wraps the rest
went around means the deer's letters are turned back to front

parts.note: an elk is a large deer
something done in the past happened long ago

indicators.note: said tells us the word is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: the word you, spoken, sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: A garment, and some confused tale of a deer circling it long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went around' turns the deer back to front, and 'without' in its old sense of outside makes it wrap the rest; 'it' is a link back to the coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagoule is a lightweight hooded waterproof jacket, a thin shell rather than a heavy overcoat.

clue.text: Risk seeing some game-keeper illicitly

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A poacher's danger: running into a gamekeeper while acting illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger, a synonym for risk; 'seeing' is a link word.

clue.text: Change one's mind and put underwear in laundry

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear
the wash is the laundry waiting to be cleaned

explanation.surface: Someone thinks again and tosses their underwear into the washing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link; the pieces simply sit side by side as the words read.
explanation.definitionFit: To indoctrinate someone is to alter their thinking by pressure, reshaping another person's mind.

clue.text: Whip out diary in hearing

indicators.note: to whip is to beat or stir up, so these letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A secret diary is snatched out during a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' as in whipping cream signals the anagram of OUT and DIARY; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditory means relating to the sense of the ear, as in a hearing test.

clue.text: Tripping, I landed on a flower

indicators.note: tripping means stumbling, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: I stumbled and fell onto a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripping' signals the anagram of I LANDED ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a yellow weed-flower with a fluffy seed head.

clue.text: Flag which is likely to make very brief appearances

annotationWithheld.why: Flag which is likely to make very brief appearances (4) for WILT: 'Flag' defines it, but no parse of the rest builds WILT from the clue words as printed (scan matches)
annotationWithheld.clue: Flag which is likely to make very brief appearances

clue.text: Casual discard

definitions.meaning: casual as in offhand, a remark made in passing
something to be thrown out after use

explanation.definitionFit: An offhand remark is a throwaway line; and a disposable item is one you bin.

clue.text: Don't forget about legislator

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a member of parliament is a legislator

explanation.surface: A reminder concerning a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: MEMBER here is a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember is to keep in mind, the opposite of letting slip.

clue.text: Landlord breaking silence over lease finally

indicators.note: breaking means the letters are broken up and rearranged
finally points to the last letter of lease

explanation.surface: A landlord breaks the quiet to talk about the lease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' shuffles SILENCE into LICENSE, and 'finally' adds E from 'lease'; 'over' sets it above in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensee holds a licence to sell alcohol, such as a pub landlord in Britain.

clue.text: Charitable stamp

definitions.meaning: stamp as in sort or type: a man of that stamp

explanation.definitionFit: Generous in nature; and a sort or type, as in 'of that ilk'.

clue.text: To fairies, woman's an annoying person

parts.note: peris are fairies or sprites of Persian legend
her is a woman's possessive, the woman's

explanation.surface: A woman offering something to the fairies turns out to be a pest.
explanation.walkthrough: A PERI is a Persian fairy, a crossword staple. 'To' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Perisher is British slang for a pest or rascal, often a mischievous child.

clue.text: A booboo students put up

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is set from bottom to top

parts.note: pupils are students

explanation.surface: Students staged a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses PUPILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: 'ave a look for a plant? Not so

parts.note: to have a look for is to hunt; with Cockney dropped h's, 'ave and 'unt
rue is a bitter herb

explanation.surface: Someone asks in Cockney whether you'll search for a plant, and gets a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h in 'ave signals that hunt loses its h too.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue means false, not the case.

clue.text: In the country, a slippery character appears self-employed

indicators.note: In means the slippery character sits inside the country's name

parts.note: France is the country in question
an eel is the proverbially slippery creature

explanation.surface: A dodgy operator in France sets up working for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a slippery character' looks like a crook but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelancer works independently for various clients rather than for one employer.

clue.text: View of expert left out in confrontation

indicators.note: left out means these letters are removed

parts.note: a face-to-face is a direct confrontation
taken as written
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert's opinion goes unheard in a confrontation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' takes OF ACE from the end of FACE-TO-FACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is an aspect or angle on a subject.

clue.text: Push and 'e's out, having encompassed a duck

parts.note: 'e is he with the h dropped, Cockney style, so just the letter E

indicators.note: having encompassed means the out holds the duck inside it

parts.note: LBW, leg before wicket, is a way of being out in cricket
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: He is dismissed after scoring nothing and shoves his way off.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is out LBW (leg before wicket), and a duck is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow is to shove or jostle someone aside.

clue.text: Spout broken right in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle means the right letter goes inside the broken word

parts.note: bust means broken

explanation.surface: A water spout broken right through the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spout' is the definition, a verb: to gush.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst forth is to gush out, as liquid does from a spout.

clue.text: Ship's barber

definitions.meaning: a fast sailing vessel of the nineteenth century, like the Cutty Sark
a barber is one who cuts hair

explanation.definitionFit: A fast tea ship with tall masts; and someone who trims hair with shears.

clue.text: 'Overspread' misspelt in Webster

indicators.note: misspelt means the letters of the name are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry wrongly spelt in Webster's dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the dictionary name Webster is what gets rearranged by 'misspelt'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestrew is to scatter things over a surface, to cover it.

clue.text: Fast-moving restorative ultimately failing to make stronger

indicators.note: failing means that letter goes missing from the strengthening phrase

parts.note: to tone up muscles is to strengthen them

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word restorative

explanation.surface: A tonic that works quickly but in the end fails to build you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes E, the last letter of 'restorative', and 'failing' removes it from TONE UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton-up is British slang for travelling at a hundred miles an hour, especially on a motorbike.

clue.text: In all seriousness, it's too soon to settle in

indicators.note: in means the settling word goes inside the other

parts.note: if it's too soon, it is early
to nest is to settle down in a home

explanation.surface: Someone protests, quite seriously, that it is too soon to move into a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's too soon' is a whole phrase standing for one word; the final 'in' is the container signal, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means sincerely and gravely, without joking.
